newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish leftist party files government censure.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leftist party files government censure.

text.p: A leading Turkish leftist party said on Wednesday it had filed a censure motion against the Islamist-led government to safeguard the country's secular system.
"We handed it (the censure proposal) to the speaker of parliament at 11 o'clock (2100 GMT) last night," a spokesman for the Democratic Left Party (DSP) told Reuters.
No date was announced for consideration of the motion. Passage would doom the seven-month-old coalition government.
Another leading leftist party, the Republican People's Party (CHP), has said it planned to file its own censure motion later on Wednesday.
"Turkey's democratic and secular republic is being exposed to a serious threat and dangerous environment in the hands of this regime," the DSP statement to the speaker of parliament said.
The statement said the ruling Islamist Welfare Party was "closing its eyes to violations of the constitutional state."

Turkey's secularists have been enraged by an anti-Israel rally in an Ankara district held by the Welfare Party last week. In an apparent show of strength by the secular army, a convoy of tanks and military vehicles paraded through the area on Tuesday.
DSP leader Bulent Ecevit said the censure motion would be supported by many members of the junior coalition partner, the conservative True Path Party (DYP).

A censure motion would need the support of other opposition parties, including the major Motherland Party, and several government deputies. The coalition has a narrow majority in the 550-seat parliament.
Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, apparently renounced his radical pro-Islam and anti-Western election pledges after forming the governing coalition last June.
But he has angered members of Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's DYP and the powerful army in recent weeks with plans to build mosques and other Islamist programmes.
